marks.gloss_en: the Sages taught: 'in sukkot you shall dwell' -- and not in a sukkah beneath a sukkah
אדרבה: בסוכות תרתי משמע -- on the contrary, the plural 'sukkot' implies two (a sukkah under a sukkah should be fit)
בסכת כתיב -- it is written without the vav (= p_basukkot_ktiv_chaser)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: it is written בסכת (without the vav) -- the written form is singular
a sukkah atop a sukkah: the upper one is fit
R' Yirmeya: sometimes both sukkot are fit, sometimes both unfit, sometimes the lower fit and the upper unfit, sometimes the lower unfit and the upper fit
both fit: the lower's sun exceeds its shade, the upper's shade exceeds its sun, and the upper stands within twenty
both unfit: in both the shade exceeds the sun, and the upper stands above twenty amot
ממאי? מדקתני כאילו עשאה בתוך הבית -- the mishnah's comparison to a house shows the tree meant is one whose shade exceeds its sunlight
this is what it teaches: a tree is like a house -- as a house's shade exceeds its sunlight, so [the tree meant] is one whose shade exceeds its sunlight
וכי חמתו מרובה מצלתו מאי הוי? הא קא מצטרף סכך פסול בהדי סכך כשר!
Rav Pappa: [Rava speaks] where he lowered them [the branches into the roofing]
Rava: they taught [this] only of a tree whose shade exceeds its sunlight
we do not decree [invalidity] where he lowered them on account of where he did not
[we learned:] if he trellised a vine, a gourd or ivy over it and roofed over them -- invalid; if the roofing exceeded them, or he cut them -- valid
(entertained) the mishnah speaks where he did not lower them
